product: Email Security Gateway and Email Gateway Defense
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read mail logs from two Barracuda sources: the Email Security Gateway appliance and Email Gateway Defense (EGD). Both send syslog to the data collector. The appliance's mail syslog lines and EGD message log records go to Email, and EGD audit records and the appliance's web syslog stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- Email Security Gateway appliance: set the syslog server under Advanced > Advanced Networking.
- Email Gateway Defense (Email Protection Advanced plan): set the syslog integration (TCP with TLS) to the data collector.

Field mapping:
- Email Security Gateway: the mail syslog's RECV, SCAN and SEND lines, one per action per recipient, go to Email with Barracuda's action and reason codes turned into names.
- Email Gateway Defense: message log records go to Email, with status, reason and threat taken from the first recipient.
- EGD audit records and the appliance's web syslog stay generic.
- A gateway status of DELIVERED on RECV and SCAN lines means the appliance let the message through; SEND lines carry the delivery result.

Time:
- SCAN and RECV lines use the Start epoch time; SEND lines use the header time, which has no zone and is read as UTC.

Sources and licenses:
- Barracuda publishes the appliance's field order and code tables but no full example line, and EGD's syslog header isn't documented, so the parent reads EGD records from the email[1]: tag to the end of the line.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up from Barracuda's field order and EGD's JSON examples.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser in that tenant matched these lines.

Known gaps:
- EGD documents attachments only as null, so attachments aren't mapped.
